newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Seven dead, 15 hurt in Colombian bloodletting.
newsitem.headline: Seven dead, 15 hurt in Colombian bloodletting.

text.p: At least seven people were killed and 15 others injured, including two children, in political bloodletting across Colombia on Tuesday, authorities said.

Unidentified gunmen dragged three men, active in Catholic Church social programmes, from their homes before dawn and shot them to death in the fishing village of Barranca Nueva in northern Bolivar province, Mayor Pedro Guerrero said.

It was not immediately known who was behind the violence although the region has witnessed a recent spate of attacks by right-wing death squads. Colleagues of the dead men, who asked not to be identified, believe the gunmen were searching for John Mahoney, a British priest who works in the community.

In a separate incident in a rural area near the town of Ituango in northwest Antioquia province, one soldier was killed and three soldiers and seven civilians were hurt when guerrillas dynamited an army truck, military sources said.
They blamed the attack on the Cuban-inspired National Liberation Army (ELN), set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966.

In the third fatal incident, gunmen shot to death two former policemen and their driver in the southwest city of Cali. Police said the motive was unclear, but two of the victims had been working as lawyers.

In the northeast oil-production centre of Barrancabermeja, ELN rebels blew up a military truck, injuring three soldiers, one civilian and two girls, one of them 6 years old, regional army chief Maj. Juan Carlos Barrera told reporters.
The attacks came just two days after the ELN shot down a helicopter in eastern Colombia, killing 20 soldiers and one civilian as they flew to repair an oil pipeline that had been blown up earlier.

In a statement late on Monday a combined right-wing paramilitary force, known as the United Self-Defence Groups of Colombia (AUC), said it was setting up a special commando to attack guerrillas that injured or killed children, the leading El Tiempo newspaper reported.
The move follows a FARC attack on a farm in northwest Antioquia province last week in which 11-year-old twin brothers died.
